instructions:
Citrello is the user's reference manager. Its library is shared across all chats and projects.

How to cite:
- Before citing, call search_references to find the reference and its key. If it is not there, call add_reference
  with the DOI (best) or the full reference text. Never invent keys or reference details.
- In any text you write (chat answers, drafts, documents), cite with markers: [@Key], several as [@Key1; @Key2],
  with a page as [@Key, p. 12], with a prefix as [see @Key], and after the author's name in a sentence as
  Smith et al. [-@Key] (shows only the year).
- To give the user a Word file, call create_word_document with your text containing markers: citations become live
  (Mendeley-compatible) fields with a formatted bibliography. Use update_word_document to restyle or refresh a .docx.
- When editing existing text, keep every citation marker exactly as it is unless asked to change citations.
- Check add_reference's reliability result and tell the user about problems (retracted paper, wrong DOI, ...).
- Use a project name (e.g. the paper's title) to keep references of one paper together.

Full texts:
- Citrello keeps the text of papers the user added (search_references shows full_text: true). To check whether a
  cited paper supports a sentence, call read_paper with the sentence as the query and quote the passage you rely on.
  find_in_papers searches inside all the user's papers. When a paper has no full text, say so instead of guessing
  from the title, and tell the user how to add it (the Citrello browser button on the paper's page, or its PDF).

LaTeX / Overleaf:
- Cite with the library keys: \cite{Key}, \citep{Key1,Key2}, \citet{Key}, or the biblatex commands \parencite / \textcite.
  Keys are the same as in [@Key] markers and never change.
- Give the user the bibliography with get_bibtex (a project or keys; format bibtex or biblatex) to save as references.bib.
- check_citations also checks \cite commands. check_latex_project checks a .tex file, folder or Overleaf .zip on disk:
  cited keys missing from the .bib, unused and duplicate entries, unreliable references, hand-typed bibliographies.
- prepare_arxiv turns a LaTeX project into an arXiv-ready .zip (with the .bbl arXiv needs) and lists what to fix.

tools.name: search_references
tools.title: Search the library
tools.description: Search the user's reference library (all chats share it) by author, title, year, DOI, key or tag. Empty query lists recent references. Returns keys to cite as [@Key].

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

tools.name: get_reference
tools.title: Show a reference
tools.description: Full details of one reference, optionally formatted in a citation style.

style.description: Citation style id, e.g. apa, ieee, nature, vancouver, harvard-cite-them-right, chicago-author-date, or any id from zotero.org/styles. Default: apa

tools.name: add_reference
tools.title: Add a reference
tools.description: Add a reference to the library from a DOI, a link to the paper (publisher page, arXiv, ScienceDirect, doi.org...) or a web page, or a full typed reference. Looks it up on Crossref, avoids duplicates, and returns its key plus a reliability check (verified / check / problem, e.g. retracted or wrong DOI).

reference.description: DOI, link, or full reference text

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

tools.name: add_references
tools.title: Add several references
tools.description: Add several references at once (DOIs or typed references).

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the user's projects (groups of references, e.g. one per paper).

tools.name: format_references
tools.title: Format references
tools.description: Format references (by keys or a whole project) in a citation style: in-text citations and the bibliography as plain text.

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

style.description: Citation style id, e.g. apa, ieee, nature, vancouver, harvard-cite-them-right, chicago-author-date, or any id from zotero.org/styles. Default: apa

tools.name: check_citations
tools.title: Check citation markers
tools.description: Check that every [@Key] marker in a text exists in the library, and list the ones that don't.

tools.name: create_word_document
tools.title: Create a Word document
tools.description: Create a Word (.docx) file from text with [@Key] markers. Supports # headings, paragraphs, - bullets, **bold**, *italic*. Citations become live fields and a bibliography is added in the chosen style. Saved to ~/Citrello/Documents unless a path is given.

style.description: Citation style id, e.g. apa, ieee, nature, vancouver, harvard-cite-them-right, chicago-author-date, or any id from zotero.org/styles. Default: apa

tools.name: update_word_document
tools.title: Update a Word document
tools.description: Update a .docx: turn [@Key] markers and typed-in markers into live citations and re-render every citation and the bibliography in a style. Overwrites the file unless output_path is given. The file is on the user's computer, opened by the Citrello app (https://citrello.app/connect).

style.description: Citation style id, e.g. apa, ieee, nature, vancouver, harvard-cite-them-right, chicago-author-date, or any id from zotero.org/styles. Default: apa

tools.name: read_paper
tools.title: Read a paper's full text
tools.description: Read the full text of a paper in the user's library (Citrello keeps the text of papers the user added). With a query (e.g. the sentence that cites it), returns the passages that match best; without, the text from the start. Shows whether a cited paper really says what a sentence claims, with the passage to quote. Only for references whose full text Citrello has (full_text: true).

query.description: What to look for, e.g. the citing sentence

max_chars.description: Without a query: how much text (default 12000)

tools.name: find_in_papers
tools.title: Search inside papers
tools.description: Search inside the full texts of the papers in the user's library (all, a project, or given keys) and return the best passage of each matching paper. Good for 'which of my papers says X?' and for finding a source for a claim.

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

tools.name: get_bibtex
tools.title: Get BibTeX
tools.description: BibTeX or biblatex entries for references (by keys, a project, or the whole library), with the same stable keys as [@Key] markers, for LaTeX / Overleaf (\cite{Key}). Returns the .bib text, or saves it when output_path is given.

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

tools.name: check_latex_project
tools.title: Check a LaTeX project
tools.description: Check a LaTeX project on disk (a .tex file, a folder, or an Overleaf source .zip): cited keys missing from the .bib (and whether they are in the library), unused and duplicate entries, unreliable references (retracted, wrong DOI, no DOI...), and hand-typed bibliographies. The project is on the user's computer, read by the Citrello app (https://citrello.app/connect).

tools.name: prepare_arxiv
tools.title: Make an arXiv-ready .zip
tools.description: Make an arXiv-ready .zip from a LaTeX project on disk (folder, Overleaf source .zip or main .tex): adds the .bbl arXiv needs (it never runs BibTeX), removes comments and build files, adds \pdfoutput=1, and reports what would make arXiv fail (missing figures, case mismatches, biblatex, citations missing from the .bib, bad file names, >50 MB). Writes <name>_arxiv.zip next to the project unless output_path is given; the project is not changed. The project is on the user's computer, read by the Citrello app (https://citrello.app/connect).

tools.name: import_zotero_library
tools.title: Import from Zotero
tools.description: Import the user's Zotero library from Zotero on this computer (no account or key needed). Zotero collections become projects; duplicates are skipped.

project.description: Also put everything into this project (optional)

tools.name: list_styles
tools.title: Find a citation style
tools.description: Find a citation style: with no query, the styles ready offline; with a journal, publisher or style name (e.g. 'Journal of Cleaner Production', 'IEEE'), matching styles from the full set of 10,000+.

tools.name: verify_references
tools.title: Verify references online
tools.description: Check references online against Crossref (all not-yet-verified ones, or given keys or a project): fixes their details from the publisher record and re-rates them as verified / check / problem (retracted, wrong DOI...). Takes about a second per reference.

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)

tools.name: import_references
tools.title: Import a reference file
tools.description: Import a RIS, BibTeX or CSL-JSON file (exported from Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote...) into the library, skipping duplicates.

project.description: Project name, e.g. the paper's title (optional)
